newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican urges U.N. force in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Vatican urges U.N. force in Zaire.

text.p: The Vatican urged the United Nations on Saturday to form a humanitarian force to ensure food and medicine distribution to starving refugees in Zaire.

Archbishop Jean-Louis Tauran, the Vatican's "foreign minister", told Vatican Radio in an interview the Holy See backed a "humanitarian corridor, militarily protected, to ensure food and aid distribution" in eastern Zaire.
"It would be opportune to set up an international force, made up of several countries through the United Nations, to confront the situation in Zaire," Tauran said.
While it was not the Vatican's duty "to give technical solutions", Tauran said "the Holy See expressed itself in favour of such a force through diplomatic channels".
Tauran also urged Rwanda's government to allow its citizens to return from Zaire "with the respective assurances" for their personal security.
"And Rwanda must call back its soldiers, who are present on Zaire's territory," he said, adding that arms sales to the African Great Lakes region must cease for peace to last.

The U.N. Security Council called on U.N. members on Saturday to lay the groundwork for a multinational force to help feed more than a million starving refugees from ethnic violence in Rwanda and Burundi.
The resolution did not authorise an immediate force, however, and it seemed there would be no respite soon for the refugees.
Meanwhile, the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) warned of mass death in the next three weeks if aid corridors were not set up.
